proposed_fix.description: Confirm cartservice is behaving erratically, then raise the CPU limit on the cartservice container only, with human approval and a ready rollback.
steps: Check whether cartservice is behaving normally and whether CPU throttling (CPUThrottlingHigh) is actually firing for the container, per R1.
Compare cartservice CPU requests and limits against observed usage (E5 shows CPU +61%) and check the node kernel version, per R1.
Check for a recent deploy, traffic increase, or connection leak that explains the socket (z=7.46) and memory (z=4.7) growth in E5.
If the throttling and erratic behavior are confirmed, request approval to raise the CPU limit on the cartservice container only, in a modest increment, leaving requests unchanged.
After rollout, watch cartservice CPU, socket count, memory, trace error rate (E2) and frontend_error (E1) for recovery.
If errors persist after CPU headroom is added, escalate to investigate the socket and memory growth as the likely root cause rather than raising limits further.
preconditions: Another alert (e.g. frontend_error from E1) is firing in the same namespace, which R1 requires before raising limits.
CPU throttling on the cartservice container is confirmed, not just high CPU usage.
The node has spare allocatable CPU for the increased limit.
A human on-call engineer has approved the change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Revert the cartservice CPU limit to its previous value by re-applying the prior deployment manifest or running a rollout undo, then confirm the pod restarts cleanly and metrics return to the pre-change baseline.

Metrics (cartservice_socket z=7.46) and traces (cartservice inbound errors 0->12.75%) both point at cartservice, and logs show gRPC error status lines only from cartservice; I have enough to finish, with socket as the fault type since it has the highest deviation and latency is not elevated, which fits a socket-level fault rather than cpu or delay.

alternatives_rejected.why: frontend_error z=20 in E1 is the downstream symptom; cartservice inbound errors rose 0->0.1275 (E2) while its self-time stayed flat (1.02x), so the failure originates at cartservice, not frontend.

cartservice_mem z=4.7 (23.5%) is weaker than cartservice_socket z=7.46 (37.3%) in E1, and nothing in E2 or E4 shows memory-specific behavior such as slowdowns or OOM; the log lines are gRPC error status codes, which fit connection failures better.
E2 shows self-time p50 essentially unchanged (4.0->4.08ms), so there is no latency or CPU saturation signature; the failure presents as errors, not slowness.
